    • 3.1 Morphological diversity based on qualitative descriptors

    • 3.3 Tabla 2: Presents descriptive statistics for the quantitative traits evaluated in the blues dataset. For each trait, the table reports the mean, minimum, maximum, coefficient of variation (CV%) and broad-sense heritability (H²), providing a summary of the central tendency, range, relative variability and genetic determination of the measured characteristics.
  • 4 Objective 2: To identify promising accessions using BLUEs of five agronomic traits and to compare five selection approaches.

2 Data import

3 Objective 1: To assess the phenotypic diversity of 144 quinoa accessions (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) under the agroecological conditions of Ayacucho, Peru, using diversity indices and repeatability estimates of qualitative traits.

3.1 Morphological diversity based on qualitative descriptors

Na = number of accessions per class; Nc = observed classes; Ne = effective number of classes; He = Nei’s diversity index; H′ = Shannon–Weaver index.

4 Objective 2: To identify promising accessions using BLUEs of five agronomic traits and to compare five selection approaches.

4.1 Data preparation

The BLUEs of five traits (SYP, TSW, PH, PLr, LOD) were used for the 144 accessions. Negative BLUEs of LOD were set to zero. Traits were rescaled to 0–1 so that higher values are always better: LOD is inverted, and PH is penalized by its distance to an optimal range (P25–P75). The top 10 % of accessions (n = 14) was retained by each method.

4.2 Principal component analysis

PCA was run on the standardized BLUEs. The first principal component, oriented so that SYP loads positively, was used as the selection score.

4.3 Elston index

The Elston (1963) index was computed with st4gi::elston(), as in the F7 selection stage of Lozano-Isla et al. (2023). It is a weight-free index on standardized trait means, so traits to be minimized (the PH penalty and LOD) are multiplied by −1 before the calculation. The index is used here with yield, plant height and lodging.

4.4 Mulamba–Mock index

Accessions were ranked for each oriented trait (rank 1 = best) and the ranks were combined as a weighted sum, with weights of 3 for SYP, 2 for TSW and 1 for the remaining traits.

4.5 Distance to the ideotype

The ideotype takes the best value of every oriented trait (maximum for SYP, TSW and PLr; P25–P75 range for PH; minimum for LOD). Accessions were scored by the negative weighted Euclidean distance to it.

4.6 Random forest

A random forest (2000 trees) predicted SYP from the other four traits. The out-of-bag prediction was used as the selection score, and permutation importance ranks the traits.

4.7 Comparison among selection methods

Agreement among methods was assessed with Spearman and Pearson correlations, the overlap of the top 10 %, and the standardized selection differential of each trait. Accessions chosen by at least three methods are reported as consensus selections.
